_note: The list of screens the accessibility run checks. bin/a11y.sh is what runs it: it
supplies the admin session and fills in the {{PLACEHOLDERS}}, which stand for ids
that do not exist until `npm run a11y:seed` has created something.
STANDARD. WCAG2AA here is the GATE -- the level this plugin commits to, and the
level at which a failure stops the run. bin/a11y.sh runs a second pass at
WCAG2AAA afterwards and prints it without failing on it, which is the 'AAA
wherever it can be achieved' half of the requirement.
RUNNERS. The axe runner is a local file, not the bundled 'axe' one. See its
header: the bundled runner reports axe's 'could not determine' results as errors,
which on this plugin meant 28 contrast failures on core's own <select> elements,
measured at about 17:1.
rootElement ON THE ADMIN SCREENS IS LOAD-BEARING, not a way of narrowing the
scan. wp-admin is behind a capability check and a login form passes an
accessibility check cleanly, so a run that had quietly lost its session would
report twenty green screens it never saw. Requiring #wpbody-content means such a
run fails instead. Verified by mutation: point it at a selector that does not
exist and 19 of 22 URLs fail.
IGNORE. Two rules are ignored, both verified against the browser's own
accessibility tree rather than argued away. docs/accessibility.md records the
evidence and how to re-check it; tests/smoke.php fails if this list and that
document stop agreeing.

urls.comment: Overview. The two cards and the counts table.
The queue, unfiltered: status badges, masked contact columns, sortable headers.
The queue filtered. A different view link carries aria-current, which nothing else renders.
The queue with a search term and no matches. The empty state is its own markup.
One recovery: the reveal link, and the four POST buttons that change it.
The editor with a workflow loaded: every step is a details panel.
The editor with nothing loaded, which is how a new workflow is started.
Integrations: cards stating status in a sentence, including unavailable ones.
Settings, one entry per tab: each is its own document and its own settings group.
A deeplinked field. The highlight, the fragment and the announcement only exist in this state.
System Status: the check tables and the Run now form.
The screen a fresh activation lands on.
Public: the opt-out page as it is presented, on a live token.
Public: the page after the opt-out button is pressed. A second token, because pa11y-ci visits concurrently and this one is consumed.
Public: what a link that does not resolve renders. Also what an expired or revoked one renders.

Public: the add-to-cart capture field, on a real product page. It WAITS for our own field rather than just loading the page: without that this entry would pass just as well with the capture point switched off, which is a screen reporting a clean check of markup it never saw.
actions: wait for element #recoveryflow-atc-phone to be visible

urls.comment: Public: the basket page's save-this-basket form. The basket is filled by pressing the real add-to-cart button, because the form only renders on a basket with something in it. The query argument is what makes this a DIFFERENT key from the product entry above: pa11y-ci reports results keyed by url, so two entries sharing one address overwrite each other and the findings of the first vanish.
